fundamental.headline: Strong business, but expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 46% over the last year, it keeps 30 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it has more cash than debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 80% of the last 5 years. It also looks pricier than similar companies once growth is considered.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
Profit margins are widening: it keeps more of each sale than a year ago.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Great business, but you're paying up for it: fine to own, better to add slowly or wait for a pullback. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 9% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 46% last year; 57%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 59% (3 years ago -6%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $59 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 107% (3 years ago -16%).

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $10.0B vs operating income $5.7B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 57%/yr over 3 years and -4%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 39% vs a 5-year range of -68–39% (median 12%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $3.2B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($3.0B buybacks + $196M dividends) = 3.3% of the company's market value. Share count up 2.1% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $40.40, up 38% in 90 days (up 27% in the last 30); 19 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $24.72, up 34% in 90 days (up 23% in the last 30); 21 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By product, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Cloud 88% of sales, up 54%; Client 7% of sales, up 119%; Consumer 4% of sales, up 19%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +161% vs a year ago · $26.10 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 161% vs sales 67%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 7 quarters running by about 11%, yet the stock fell after 4 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 67% from a year ago and speeding up (from 45% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $39 of operating profit, up from $28 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Just 43% of reported profit became spare cash: much of the profit is tied up in spending or working capital.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 10× last year's profit (lower than 57% of the last 5 years); only 7× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 28; analysts expect EPS of $5.87, up 176% from a year ago. It usually moves about 7% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 38% in 90 days (19 raised, 0 cut lately): forecasts are moving up fast.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
